title: Summarize Services Provided by Networked Hosts

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A network contains more than client computers. Many hosts exist specifically to provide services to other devices.
Networked hosts can resolve names, assign addresses, share resources, provide applications, centralize logs and identity, filter or distribute traffic, and monitor connected physical systems.
bullets: Server roles: DNS, DHCP, fileshare, print, mail, syslog, web, AAA, database, and NTP
Internet appliances: spam gateway, UTM, load balancer, and proxy
sections.callout: Ask: what service is this host providing to the network?

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a scenario describes what a networked system is doing, can you identify the server role, appliance, industrial system, or IoT device responsible?
bullets: Shared resources → file or print server

sections.title: Server Roles
paragraphs: A server role describes a service a networked host provides to other systems. One physical or virtual server can perform one role or several roles.
Focus on the service being provided, not the server's brand or operating system.

sections.title: DNS Server
paragraphs: A Domain Name System (DNS) server translates human-readable names into network information such as IP addresses. When users can connect by address but not hostname, name resolution is the clue.
sections.callout: Resolve network names → DNS server.

sections.title: DHCP Server
paragraphs: A Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server automatically provides client network settings such as an IP address, subnet information, default gateway, and DNS server information.
sections.callout: A new client automatically receives network settings → DHCP server.

sections.title: DNS vs. DHCP

table.caption: Core infrastructure services
rows: Helps devices locate resources by name

sections.callout: DHCP gives you an address; DNS helps you find an address.

sections.title: File Server and Fileshare
paragraphs: A file server stores data that users or systems access across a network. A fileshare exposes authorized folders or files for department storage, shared documents, home folders, and collaboration.
sections.callout: Employees access the same network folder → file server/fileshare.

sections.title: Print Server
paragraphs: A print server centralizes printer availability, sharing, print queues, and job management instead of making every workstation manage every printer independently.
sections.callout: Many users send jobs to a centrally managed queue → print server.

sections.title: Mail Server
paragraphs: A mail server provides organizational email services, which can include sending, receiving, storing mailboxes, and giving users access to messages.
SMTP, POP3, and IMAP describe mail protocols; this objective asks you to recognize the host providing the overall email service.
sections.callout: Organization hosts employee email → mail server.

sections.title: Syslog Server
paragraphs: Syslog provides a standardized way for routers, switches, servers, firewalls, and other devices to send log messages to a centralized location.
Central collection simplifies monitoring, troubleshooting, and event correlation.
sections.callout: Centralized logs from many network devices → syslog server.

sections.title: Web Server
paragraphs: A web server hosts websites or web applications and responds to HTTP or HTTPS requests. It can provide public sites, intranet pages, web apps, and management interfaces.
sections.callout: A browser requests the company intranet → web server.

sections.title: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA)

entries.title: Authentication
paragraphs: Authentication verifies identity using accepted credentials such as a password or certificate.

entries.title: Authorization
paragraphs: Authorization determines which resources or actions an authenticated identity is permitted to access.
entries.recognitionCue: What are you allowed to do?

entries.title: Accounting
paragraphs: Accounting records activity, sessions, connections, or resource use.

sections.callout: Authentication → identity; authorization → permissions; accounting → activity records.

sections.title: Database Server
paragraphs: A database server stores and manages structured data that applications query, insert, modify, or delete, such as customer records, inventory, orders, and account data.
sections.callout: An application queries centralized structured records → database server.

sections.title: File Server vs. Database Server
sections.callout: Shared spreadsheet file → file server; application searches customer records → database server.

sections.title: Network Time Protocol (NTP)
paragraphs: Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronizes clocks across networked systems. Accurate time supports logs, authentication, security events, troubleshooting, and scheduled operations.
When devices disagree about time, reconstructing an event sequence becomes difficult.
sections.callout: Inconsistent system timestamps → investigate NTP.

sections.title: Internet Appliances
paragraphs: Internet appliances are network devices designed primarily for specialized network or security functions. Objective 2.3 includes spam gateways, unified threat management, load balancers, and proxy servers.

sections.title: Spam Gateway
paragraphs: A spam gateway inspects email traffic and filters unwanted or malicious messages before they reach the organization's mail system or users.
sections.callout: Filter unwanted email before delivery → spam gateway.

sections.title: Unified Threat Management (UTM)
paragraphs: A unified threat management (UTM) appliance combines multiple security capabilities into one platform, potentially including firewall, intrusion detection or prevention, malware protection, and content filtering.
sections.callout: Several network-security functions in one appliance → UTM.

sections.title: Load Balancer
paragraphs: A load balancer distributes incoming requests or workloads among multiple backend servers. It can improve scalability and availability by avoiding dependence on one overloaded or unavailable server.
bullets: Clients send requests to one service
Requests are distributed across available backend servers
sections.callout: One service, multiple backend servers, distributed traffic → load balancer.

sections.title: Proxy Server
paragraphs: A proxy server acts as an intermediary between a client and another destination. It can support filtering, access control, caching, privacy, and logging.
sections.callout: Client traffic passes through a middleman → proxy server.

sections.title: Internet Appliance Comparisons

entries.title: Proxy vs. Load Balancer
paragraphs: A proxy intermediates or controls communication. A load balancer distributes requests among backend servers.

entries.title: Spam Gateway vs. UTM
paragraphs: A spam gateway specializes in email filtering. A UTM combines multiple network-security functions.

sections.callout: Proxy = middleman; load balancer = traffic distributor; spam gateway = mail specialist; UTM = consolidated security.

sections.title: Legacy and Embedded Systems
paragraphs: Not every networked system resembles a desktop or conventional server. Legacy, embedded, and industrial systems can have specialized hardware and software, limited upgrade options, and long service lifecycles.
Treat these purpose-built systems according to their operational role and constraints.

sections.title: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)
paragraphs: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems monitor and control industrial processes and infrastructure in manufacturing, utilities, water, energy, and similar environments.
SCADA can supervise sensors, pumps, machinery, and physical processes, so failures may affect production, infrastructure, or safety.
sections.callout: Networked industrial monitoring or control → SCADA.

sections.title: Internet of Things (IoT) Devices
paragraphs: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are network-connected devices with specialized functions beyond traditional general-purpose computers, such as smart thermostats, lights, cameras, sensors, appliances, and environmental monitors.
They often combine embedded hardware and software, limited local interfaces, and dependence on applications or cloud services.
sections.callout: A specialized physical device becomes network-connected → IoT.

sections.title: SCADA vs. IoT
sections.callout: Factory control → SCADA; smart connected thing → IoT.

File server → files; print server → printers

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Host a website or web app → web server
Verify identity, grant permissions, track activity → AAA
Distribute requests across servers → load balancer
Intermediary for client traffic → proxy server

sections.title: Objective 2.3 Exam Trap
paragraphs: The exam may describe the job without naming the server or appliance. Ignore what the box looks like and identify the service behavior first.

entries.title: DNS vs. DHCP
paragraphs: DNS resolves names; DHCP assigns network configuration.

entries.title: File Server vs. Database
paragraphs: Files and folders point to a file server; structured records queried by an application point to a database server.

entries.title: Authentication vs. Authorization vs. Accounting
paragraphs: Authentication verifies identity, authorization determines permissions, and accounting tracks activity.

entries.title: Syslog vs. NTP
paragraphs: Logs point to syslog; time synchronization points to NTP. Synchronized time also makes centralized logs more useful.

entries.title: Spam Gateway vs. Mail Server
paragraphs: A mail server provides email; a spam gateway filters unwanted or malicious email.

entries.title: Proxy vs. Load Balancer
paragraphs: A proxy intermediates or filters communication; a load balancer spreads incoming requests across backend servers.

entries.title: SCADA vs. IoT
paragraphs: Industrial process control points to SCADA; a specialized connected device points to IoT.

sections.callout: SERVICE BEHAVIOR → SERVER OR APPLIANCE ROLE.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Spread traffic across servers → load balancer
